_intro:
## Read this first (checked by eye, 2026-11-02, about 2,500 noon images, kinds only: no walkable cells yet)

**The square-on fault distorts the ranking below.** Until the capture changed on 2026-11-02, pictures faced walls exactly square (344 kinds, and all cells look along axis-aligned streets). Within a few degrees of square-on, walls and panes lose their colour and interior. The same shop at 8° off is peach and lilac with a full interior, instead of pale with milky glass (`shots/sweep/objects/bld-townhouse-oldtown-flat-shop/12_10m.jpg` against `shots/sweep-check/off8/objects/bld-townhouse-oldtown-flat-shop/12_10m.jpg`). So glass, wall, lighting and blank-panel scores are all inflated for kinds shot so far. From now on the capture stands 8° off. Those kinds get shot and judged again after the fault is fixed.

**Ready for a fix session, in this order:**
1. `wall-material-differs-by-distance`: the square-on fault. A real bug, reproduced, and it matters most because it also hides other flaws. A walker sees a wall flash when looking straight at it.
2. `sky-specks-dots`: white specks at noon in the sky and in front of facades. Seen in most of the pictures I opened. Known item, probably cheap.
3. `decals-cracks-stains-pasted`: black squiggle cracks on plaster at 3 m, and the same squiggles on harbour rock.
4. `people-mannequin-stiff-blank`: close up, hair strips and hat brims turn into huge spikes, and faces are crude. Large job.
5. `props-lowpoly-blobs`: real but too broad for one session. Start with the worst seen: ice-cream scoops and vendor, surfboards as plain boxes, faceted barrels.

**Hold until the fault is fixed and these are judged again:** `glass-flat-no-depth` (its reflection over interior part is real: cars and see-through people inside rooms, `objects/bldback-office/12_1m`), `lighting-inconsistent-noon`, `blank-panels-missing-texture`.

**Hold until walkable cells are judged:** ground, foliage, roofs, fittings, architectural details, contact shadows. These look real in places, but the judges score harshly: a plain bench at 1 m got a 5, and street views like `objects/cs-text-column/12_10m` look good to me.

**Not the city:** `camera-misses-subject` and `camera-clips-into-geometry` are mostly the capture tool framing badly.

wall-material-differs-by-distance.title: Walls and panes lose their colour and interior when seen within a few degrees of square-on
wall-material-differs-by-distance.checked: READY. Real, reproduced at 0° and 1° off, gone at 8°, at 1–10 m, in hard-edged rectangles that shift with the angle. Also with the running city and a fresh load. Stays with nonear, noclosemat, noclosewin, nofacbake, nowallrelief, nomassing. nowinreveal was captured but its picture was not opened. Close-materials then tints the white, which is probably the cyan mortar
wall-material-differs-by-distance.owner: buildings wall shader, src/world/buildings/materials.ts (cause not found). Cost unknown; likely small once found

sky-specks-dots.checked: READY. Real: white dots at noon in the sky and in front of facades and glass, so not only stars
sky-specks-dots.owner: not traced; sky or particles. Known item. Probably small

decals-cracks-stains-pasted.checked: READY. Real: black squiggle cracks on plaster at 3 m (kiosk, apartment) and on harbour rock (harbor-fishquay-netheap at 1 m)
decals-cracks-stains-pasted.owner: wear patterns: src/world/buildings/materials.ts, closemat crack tile. Rock not traced. Medium

people-mannequin-stiff-blank.checked: READY. Real at 1–3 m: hair strips and hat brims become huge spikes, faces crude, a see-through dither near the lens. The capture exaggerates it by standing in the crowd

props-lowpoly-blobs.checked: READY, but split it. Real: ice-cream scoops and vendor, surfboards as boxes, faceted barrels. The judges overrate some: a plain bench at 1 m got a 5
props-lowpoly-blobs.owner: props and vendor kits. Large overall; do it kit by kit

glass-flat-no-depth.checked: HOLD. Milky panes at 10 m were largely the square-on fault. Reflection over interior is real: cars and see-through people inside rooms (bldback-office at 1 m)
glass-flat-no-depth.owner: window and room shaders. Judge again after the fault is fixed

lighting-inconsistent-noon.checked: HOLD. Partly the square-on fault. Sunlit views look right, but shaded walls do read dim and bluish at noon (bldback-townhouse at 3 m). Not exposure: the meter only changes it by up to 30 %
lighting-inconsistent-noon.owner: sky ambient level. Judge again after the fault is fixed

blank-panels-missing-texture.checked: HOLD. Not opened one by one; likely inflated by the square-on fault
blank-panels-missing-texture.owner: Judge again after the fault is fixed

ground-surfaces-flat.checked: HOLD. Gravel at 1 m is real: it reads as pebbled carpet. Many other lines are weak
ground-surfaces-flat.owner: closemat loose ground. Wait for walkable cells

foliage-flat-cards.checked: HOLD. Real on the back-garden bank (bldback-house at 10 m): flat leaf clumps on near-black ground. Lawn at 10 m is acceptable

roofs-walls-bare-uniform.checked: HOLD. One picture: the flat roof terrace is a plain tan slab, tiles look blotchy

camera-misses-subject.checked: NOT THE CITY, mostly. Sampled lines: the capture misses the subject, or a wall blocks the view

camera-clips-into-geometry.checked: NOT THE CITY, mostly. Sampled lines: the camera is against a wall or a passer-by's head. A few misfiled lines may be real (feat-footbridge)
